Proposed next steps (we can run these as a short compatibility sprint):
1) Smoke tests against Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint using your existing prompt set (you already flagged ~120 representative prompts).
2) SDK swap validation — we provide a quick code snippet and test harness to run end-to-end calls from your integration.
3) Prompt-diff analysis (we'll capture outputs and flag top regressions by intent).
4) Performance check on average 500 concurrent sessions (we'll simulate with burst profile).

Deliverables we'll provide by Friday:
- Migration test plan (attached)
- OpenAI-compat mapping doc + SDK snippets (Dylan will follow up)
- A comparison spreadsheet template so you can record top diffs and severity

Can you share the prompt set and a preferred window for a 30-minute smoke test later this week? If you want we can run the first pass with our test account and share results.

Hi Sarah —

Quick answers and plan from the SE side. Short version: OpenAI-compatible mode is intentionally close, but there are a few mapping and behavioral notes to validate.

Rate limits / bursts:
- Default: 60 reqs/min with 20 concurrent streaming connections for the compatibility endpoint.
- For the smoke run we can temporarily set a burst quota (up to 500 concurrent) — we'll need an IP list or test harness to lock to.

Tokenization:
- Redwood uses the same tokenizer family we ship for the OpenAI-compatible models; differences usually come from model-spec and truncation strategy. We recommend testing with the exact prompt set and capturing both token counts and outputs.

API/SDK swap notes (high level):
- Header mapping: keep Authorization: Bearer <key>. Redwood accepts the same model names we advertised, but client SDKs will require swapping import to @redwoodai/sdk in one line.
- Streaming semantics match; however Redwood's chunking includes incremental metadata headers (x-rdwd-chunk-id) — no change required for common clients but note for low-level parsers.

Recommended tests (we can run these):
1) Prompt parity: run the 120 prompts, store responses, compute BLEU/ROUGE and intent match percentages.
2) Edge cases: long-context prompts > 2048 tokens and truncated response behavior.
3) Latency/throughput smoke: 30-min simulation of 500 concurrent sessions with burst profile for 5 minutes.

I've attached a short compatibility guide and a prompts-diff checklist. If you can share an API key for a temporarily scoped test key (or we can run from our test harness and share logs) we'll kick off step 1 tomorrow.

Attachments: openai-compat-guide.md, prompts-diff-guidelines.txt

—Dylan
